summary: Cross-cutting change with the load-bearing escalation logic moving across a process boundary (host /sdlc -> agent-side overseer). The architect has taken the major risks identified in the v1 risk pass and converted them into concrete deliverables: filed-issues schema is now JSONL append-only (cures the corrupt-on-partial-write risk), the /sdlc overseer-absent fallback is in component_breakdown as a real deliverable (cures the silent-host risk), the infra-error helper is extracted into shared/egg_overseer_helpers/infra_error.py (cures the prompt-vs-Python regex duplication), and the agent-side CLI is a true decision-9 opt-1 (cures the v1 mis-routing through an orchestrator endpoint). Five risks remain with substantial residual exposure and require explicit planner attention: (1) the architect pinned overseer_advisor_model to 'claude-opus-4-20250514' which is the OLDER Opus 4 May-2025 generation, NOT the claude-opus-4-6 the egg codebase already canonicalizes (shared/egg_harness/config.py:17) AND the only model the public advisor tool currently supports -- ship-blocking unless changed; (2) the new EGG_PIPELINE_REPO env var the gateway --repo restriction depends on does not exist anywhere in the codebase today (verified by grep) and requires explicit injection in kubernetes_spawner.py / sandbox/entrypoint.py; (3) decision-19's 'no advisor budget cap' resolution leaves Opus exposure unbounded per phase; (4) host-migration regression risk against PR #2011 / #2016 calibration is real even with the threshold-as-config approach; (5) shadow-mode HITL noise + dedup-signature ambiguity create operator-fatigue and dedup-correctness risk. None of these block the plan from passing review; each needs a specific mitigation lined up before the implement phase commits to a wire shape.

risks.title: EGG_PIPELINE_REPO env var the gateway --repo restriction depends on does NOT exist anywhere today
risks.description: The architect's plan says the gateway's apply_overseer_issue_create_overrides reads env EGG_PIPELINE_REPO to enforce 'allowed repos = pipeline's own only.' Verified by grep -rn EGG_PIPELINE_REPO across sandbox/, orchestrator/, gateway/, shared/ -- ZERO references. The architect added a 'verify and inject' task in component_breakdown but flagged the planner has to confirm whether kubernetes_spawner.py needs the injection added. If the injection is missing, the gateway --repo restriction has no source-of-truth and either (a) blocks all overseer issue filing (env not set, default-deny) or (b) silently allows cross-repo filing (env not set, default-allow).
evidence: grep -rn 'EGG_PIPELINE_REPO' /home/egg/repos/egg/{sandbox,orchestrator,gateway,shared} -> zero matches (verified 2026-04-25)
Architect component_breakdown 'EGG_PIPELINE_REPO env injection' explicitly says 'Planner must run grep ... to verify whether kubernetes_spawner.py already injects it'
Existing env injections in kubernetes_spawner.py: EGG_AGENT_ROLE, EGG_PIPELINE_ID, EGG_REPO_PATH (per architect notes)
risks.blast_radius: If the env var is missing AND the gateway defaults to deny, overseer issue filing is broken at gateway layer (silent regression). If the gateway defaults to allow, cross-repo filing is possible (security regression -- overseer in pipeline-A files an issue in pipeline-B's repo).
mitigations: The implement phase MUST add EGG_PIPELINE_REPO to kubernetes_spawner.py's env block (gateway/orchestrator boundary). The architect sized this at +10 LOC; it's not optional.
The gateway MUST default-deny when EGG_PIPELINE_REPO is unset (i.e., reject the issue create with a clear error pointing at the missing env var). Default-allow is too dangerous.
Add a gateway test asserting that 'gh issue create' from overseer with EGG_PIPELINE_REPO unset returns a 4xx with a diagnostic message naming the missing env var.
Add a sandbox/entrypoint.py test asserting that EGG_PIPELINE_REPO is exported into the agent's env when the orchestrator-side spawner sets it.

Belt-and-suspenders: also verify that when gh runs WITHOUT --repo flag in the overseer container, gh's auto-detect (from CWD's git remote) lands on the pipeline's repo (since the sandbox CWD is the pipeline checkout). This is the actual safety net.
risks.rollback: If the env injection is incorrect, the gateway can be temporarily relaxed to read EGG_REPO_PATH (existing) and infer the repo from there, until the correct injection lands. Not ideal but functional.
risks.human_review_question: Confirm: gateway should default-DENY (reject the issue create with a diagnostic error) when EGG_PIPELINE_REPO is unset, NOT default-allow. This protects against spawner-injection bugs causing cross-repo filing.

risks.title: Advisor budget cap explicitly deferred (decision-19) creates unbounded Opus exposure per pipeline
risks.description: The contract resolution for decision-19 is 'no cap for now; follow-up issue tracks advisor budget specifically.' Combined with decision-18's intersection gate (Haiku confidence > 0.8 AND Tier-1 alert present), invocation rate is bounded but not capped. A genuinely stuck pipeline that keeps tripping the gate could call Opus on every cycle for the lifetime of the phase. With overseer_poll_interval_seconds=30 default and a phase that runs 10-60 minutes, that's 20-120 Opus calls per phase. At ~600 advisor output tokens (Anthropic's typical figure) plus echoing the distilled summary (decision-20: classification + 10 progress events + active health alerts + 50 log lines, est ~3-5K input tokens p95), Opus cost is non-trivial: a single bad phase could spend ~$5-25 of advisor cost, multiplied across concurrent pipelines.
evidence: Contract decision-19 resolution: 'Other: no cap for now -- we'll handle budget separately.'
Existing budget knob max_llm_cost_per_hour=$5.00 (sandbox/agent-config/rules/overseer.md:214) is per-overseer-instance and a self-monitor alert, not a hard limit.
decision-18's intersection gate bounds invocation rate but does not eliminate it -- a genuinely stuck phase will keep tripping the gate.
Anthropic note: 'Priority Tier on Sonnet does NOT cascade to Opus' -- advisor latency may extend overseer cycle time, compounding cost via slower error detection.
Architect's regression_risks_to_flag_for_risk_analyst[6]: 'Token-budget for the advisor call ... is currently estimated at 3-5K input tokens at p95 in td-3 but is UNVERIFIED'
risks.blast_radius: Per-pipeline Opus burn. Single bad pipeline could spend $5-25 of advisor cost in one phase. Across multiple concurrent pipelines this compounds.
mitigations: Add a defensive per-phase soft cap in the implement phase even though decision-19 deferred a formal cap. Recommend overseer_advisor_max_uses_per_phase with default 5 (high enough to not bite normal use; low enough to catch runaway). DOC-link the follow-up budget issue per decision-19.

Track advisor calls in the existing self_monitor max_llm_cost_per_hour budget so the cost is visible in OVERSEER_ALERT self-reports. This is mandatory cost-tracking telemetry per the architect's key_constraints.
Add an OVERSEER_ALERT anomaly type 'advisor-budget-exceeded' that fires when a per-phase soft cap is hit -- visibility, not enforcement, until the formal policy lands.

Surface advisor cost in pipeline status responses so the human can see runaway pipelines from the dashboard. The architect's metrics_for_success.instrumentation already includes token_usage in the structured log line; piggy-back on that.

If implementing per-phase max_uses, BLOCK further advisor invocations after the cap (don't gracefully degrade -- a hard stop is the right cost protection). The overseer can still emit OVERSEER_ALERT alerts via Haiku-only path.
risks.rollback: Set overseer_advisor_max_uses_per_phase=0 to disable advisor calls entirely. Reverts to today's behavior.

Risk pass strongly recommends shipping a soft cap -- deferring entirely is a single-bad-phase -> multi-$10 exposure that compounds across concurrent pipelines.

risks.title: Shadow-mode HITL gating (decision-10) could overwhelm operator with file-issue prompts
risks.description: decision-10 chose 'shadow mode first' specifically so the human approves each filing. decision-21 reinforces this: advisor returns recommendation=file_issue, OVERSEER_ALERT surfaces it, human gates via existing pending_decisions. The dedup mechanism (decision-5 + per-repo agent:overseer + anomaly-type signature) only fires at file-time, AFTER the human has already seen and acted on the HITL prompt -- meaning the human sees a HITL prompt for every advisor-recommended candidate, even ones that would have been deduped to an existing live issue.
evidence: Architect's recommended_approach.execution_flow_per_cycle step 5b: '... else egg-orch overseer alert (with detail.recommendation="file_issue") + register HITL decision via mcp__sdlc__register_open_question with options ["File now", "Skip", "Modify and file"]'
Existing pending_decisions surface (skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:642+): operator already sees decision prompts; piling more on increases triage cost.
Today's overseer fires multiple OVERSEER_ALERTs per pipeline (recent calibration in PR #2011 reduced false positives but did not eliminate them).
Issue body composition involves Opus advisor cost + HITL latency -- if the human skips/rejects, both are wasted.
risks.blast_radius: Operator fatigue. Could lead to humans approving 'file_issue' decisions reflexively without reading, which neutralizes the shadow-mode benefit. Or rejecting reflexively, which makes the feature appear broken and stalls calibration data.
mitigations: Run dedup BEFORE composing the HITL prompt: if a matching open issue already exists in .egg-state/oversight/filed-issues.jsonl OR in `gh issue list --label agent:overseer --search <signature>`, skip the HITL altogether (the OVERSEER_ALERT alone suffices). The architect's execution_flow step 5a already specifies this for the local jsonl check; extend to gh issue list BEFORE the HITL register, not at file-time.
Bundle multiple advisor recommendations into one pending_decision when they fire in rapid succession (multi-decision batching is already a pattern in skills/sdlc/SKILL.md:642).

Show the would-be issue title + body preview in the HITL prompt so humans can evaluate fast -- not just 'file an issue?'. The architect's HITL options ['File now', 'Skip', 'Modify and file'] support this; the prompt body MUST include the title + body preview, not just the question.

Track approval rate and surface in success metrics (per feedback-1.Q6: >=70% acceptance rate is the bar). If approval rate < 50% during shadow mode, advisor prompt or trigger gating needs tuning before going live.
risks.rollback: Disable auto-issue filing entirely via the off knob (R-COMPAT-05). Falls back to OVERSEER_ALERT-only.

risks.title: filed-issues.jsonl periodic compaction is O(n) reads/rewrites of the entire file
risks.description: The architect's revised schema is JSON Lines append-only (.jsonl) with a periodic compaction once per UTC day that 'reads, filters, rewrites the whole file once per day'. While typical writes are O(1) O_APPEND + fsync, the compaction is O(n) where n is the file size. If the overseer files even 10 issues per day across all pipelines, the file grows ~10 lines/day; over a month that's 300 lines, ~50 KB. Not a problem. But if shadow-mode rollout reveals high recommendation rates, file growth could outpace compaction. The compaction operation also requires a tmp+rename atomic pattern; if the writer crashes mid-compaction, the file could be partially-truncated.
evidence: Architect's component_breakdown agent-side state files: 'Eviction: drop filed-issues.jsonl lines older than 30 days at NEXT-write time (the writer reads, filters, rewrites the whole file once per day -- eviction is therefore a periodic compaction, NOT a per-write op; the typical write path remains O_APPEND).'
JSON Lines is robust to partial-line corruption (last line is dropped on parse error) but tmp+rename atomicity for compaction depends on filesystem fsync semantics.
risks.blast_radius: Compaction races with writes could lose a single record (last appended line). Worst case: file is partially-truncated and dedup state for one cycle is wrong.
mitigations: Use the standard tmp+rename pattern: write the compacted contents to filed-issues.jsonl.tmp, fsync, atomic rename. The architect's component_breakdown specifies this.

Take an exclusive flock during compaction so concurrent writers serialize (fcntl.LOCK_EX). The architect's writer spec mentions 'file-locking with O_APPEND + fsync for filed-issues.jsonl' -- ensure the implement phase actually implements the lock.
Add a sandbox/tests test that simulates concurrent writes during compaction and asserts no records are lost.
On read, validate JSON parseability per line; if a line fails to parse, skip it (don't fail the whole file).
Bound file growth: if the file exceeds N lines (e.g., 10000) without a compaction triggering, force a synchronous compaction. Prevents pathological growth in high-recommendation-rate scenarios.
risks.rollback: If compaction proves fragile, switch to time-windowed file rotation: filed-issues-2026-04.jsonl, filed-issues-2026-05.jsonl, etc. Reads concatenate the windows.

risks.title: Two coexisting overseer paths risk drift if dead-code template stays as canonical source
risks.description: The codebase has two overseer paths today: deployed sandbox/agent-config/rules/overseer.md (LLM agent) and dormant orchestrator/overseer/{monitor,classifier,decision_maker,issue_filer}.py (~3000 LOC dead code). evidence: Architect's component 'Issue filer (existing dead-code module): freeze template literal then mark unused': 'extend _build_issue_body template (lines 86-107) with explicit-links section -- so the template literal stays the canonical source even though the live caller is the new sandbox-side helper'
Architect's component 'Sandbox-side issue-body builder helper': 'Imports the existing template from orchestrator/overseer/issue_filer.py:_build_issue_body OR re-implements the same template inline'

Re-implementation OR cross-cutting import from sandbox/ to orchestrator/ both create coupling failures: cross-cutting import means sandbox at runtime depends on the orchestrator package being present (sandbox containers don't ship orchestrator/); re-implementation means two copies of the template

If the architect's 'OR re-implements the same template inline' option is chosen, add a CI lint rule that diffs the two template literals and fails if they drift.

Update test_overseer_issue_filer.py to assert the template content matches a snapshot file; sandbox/tests does the same. Snapshot-test approach catches drift even if the live caller doesn't import from the canonical source.
When the dead-code cleanup follow-up issue lands, the shared/ template becomes the only source -- this PR sets up that endgame.

risks.title: /sdlc overseer-absent fallback fires AT MOST ONCE per phase but lacks an 'I've already alerted you' state
risks.description: The architect added a concrete fallback to /sdlc: 'TRIGGER: count==0 OVERSEER_ALERTs received this phase AND phase_elapsed_seconds > 2 * overseer_stall_threshold_seconds AND running_agents non-empty -> emit one AskUserQuestion with options [Wait / Check container health / Cancel]; fires AT MOST ONCE per phase.' But the 'fires at most once per phase' invariant requires per-phase memory in the host. /sdlc is invoked fresh per host-side event-loop tick; without state it would fire on every tick.
evidence: Architect's component_breakdown skills/sdlc/SKILL.md additions: 'NEW: Overseer-absent safety net -- The fallback check fires AT MOST ONCE per phase to avoid noise.'
skills/sdlc/SKILL.md is a host-side skill spec; the host runs Claude Code which loops the skill per event tick.
Per-phase memory in the host today is the in-memory map of {role: {phase, ...}} that the architect's plan REMOVES (migrating to overseer-side agent-timing.json).
risks.blast_radius: Fallback fires on every tick during overseer-absent windows -> operator sees the same AskUserQuestion repeatedly. Defeats the 'at most once per phase' goal.
mitigations: Specify HOW the host remembers 'I've already fired the fallback this phase'. Options: (a) write a sentinel to .egg-state/oversight/sdlc-fallback-fired.json (host writes; orchestrator clears on phase transition); (b) check message_store for the AskUserQuestion the host sent; (c) read the orchestrator's current phase + a host-side in-memory cache keyed on (pipeline_id, phase). The architect's plan needs to commit to one of these in the implement phase.
Test: simulate overseer-absent for 2 consecutive ticks; assert the AskUserQuestion fires exactly once.
Surface the fallback firing in the structured log line so the human can audit.

If the fallback's de-duplication is hard to get right, accept that it fires once per host event-loop tick and add a host-side rate-limit (e.g., backoff after the first fire so subsequent ticks suppress for 5 minutes).
risks.rollback: If de-dup fails, the operator sees noisy AskUserQuestions; mitigate via rate-limit instead of strict once-per-phase.

Add a test in gateway/tests/ that asserts issue_number is correctly parsed from --json output.
Pin gh CLI version in the sandbox Dockerfile and bump deliberately.
If parsing fails, fall back to per-repo GitHub search by signature; log a self-monitor warning.
